b.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's check_delivery_date tool.

SUB · Check delivery date: When Executed by Another Workflow, inputs date (string) and area (string), then a Code node:

const areas = ['bodija','mokola','ring road','akobo','jericho'];
const holidays = ['2026-10-01','2026-12-25','2026-12-26'];
const { date, area } = $input.first().json;
const d = new Date(date + 'T12:00:00');
const a = (area || '').trim().toLowerCase();
if (isNaN(d)) return [{ json: { error: 'Date must be YYYY-MM-DD' } }];
let reason = 'ok';
if (!areas.includes(a)) reason = 'area not covered';
else if (d.getDay() === 0) reason = 'no Sunday delivery';
else if (holidays.includes(date)) reason = 'public holiday';
return [{ json: { delivers: reason === 'ok', date, area, reason } }];

Tool name: check_delivery_date. Description: "Checks whether Harvest Lane delivers to one area on one date. Use it whenever a customer asks about delivery on a day or to a place, before answering. Returns delivers (true/false) and a reason. Not for delivery fees." Inputs: date: "the delivery date as YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2026-10-05"; area: "one area name as the customer wrote it, e.g. Akobo".

Add today's date to the system message (Today is {{ $now.toFormat('yyyy-MM-dd, cccc') }}) so "tomorrow" and "Sunday" become real dates.

Expected: "Akobo on Sunday?" → tool returns no Sunday delivery → "We deliver to Akobo Monday to Saturday, not Sunday." "Lekki tomorrow?" → area not covered → "Sorry, we don't deliver to Lekki; we cover Bodija, Mokola, Ring Road, Akobo and Jericho."
mistakes: Not giving the agent today's date, so "tomorrow" and "Sunday" are turned into the wrong YYYY-MM-DD.
Hard-coding the answer in the system message, so the agent answers correctly without ever calling the tool.
An input description with no format or example, so the model sends "next Sunday" instead of a date.
Case-sensitive area matching, so "akobo" fails while "Akobo" works.
b.pass: Both test questions get correct answers (Akobo: no, because Sunday; Lekki: no, area not covered) and both traces show a check_delivery_date call with a properly formatted date; the description passes all Card 3 checks.
b.redo: Send it back if either trace lacks the tool call, the date argument is wrong or unformatted, or the description fails any checklist item.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's customer lookup from 3.5, turned into a tool.

SUB · Customer lookup: When Executed by Another Workflow, one input phone (string). Google Sheets reads Customers, a Code node normalises the number to 234… and returns one small item:

{ "found": true, "name": "Mama Bisi Kitchen", "type": "restaurant",
  "area": "Bodija", "last_order": "2026-09-28", "orders_count": 14 }
// or
{ "found": false }

Tool: Call n8n Workflow, name get_customer. Description: "Looks up one Harvest Lane customer by phone number. Use it when the staff member asks about a specific customer's details, area or last order. Returns found, name, type, area, last order date and order count. Not for prices or delivery rules." Input phone: {{ $fromAI('phone', 'the customer phone number, digits only, e.g. 08031234567', 'string') }}. Test data only: fictional customers.

QuestionShould call?Called?
Who is 08031234567?YesYes
When did 0803 123 4567 last order?YesYes
Which area is +2348055550000 in?YesYes
Is 08099990000 a hotel or a restaurant?YesYes
How many orders has 08031234567 placed?YesYes
What time do we open on Saturday?NoNo
What's 3 × ₦12,500?NoNo (calculator)

7 of 7 correct choices: 5 calls, 0 false calls.
mistakes: Forgetting to define the inputs on the "When Executed by Another Workflow" trigger, so the tool receives nothing.
Returning the whole sheet or every column instead of a few fields.
Choosing two "don't need it" questions that are so unrelated they prove nothing; one should be close (a price or hours question).
Using real customer phone numbers and names in the test data.
s.pass: A sub-workflow with a defined-input trigger, attached as a Call n8n Workflow tool with a description that passes all checks, and a table of seven questions whose traces show the tool called on all five relevant ones and on neither of the other two.
s.redo: Send it back if any relevant question skipped the tool, either irrelevant question triggered it, there are no trace screenshots, or real customer data appears.

g.answer:
Worked example: a fictional salon in Enugu, "Coal City Braids", booking helper with four tools.

ToolTypeJob
get_service_priceOwn workflowPrice and duration for one style
check_free_slotsOwn workflowFree times for one date
get_salon_infoSheets toolHours, address, payment
calculatorCalculatorTotals for several services

12 questions, three per tool. First run:

Tool targetedRight tool chosen
get_service_price3/3
check_free_slots1/3
get_salon_info3/3
calculator2/3
Total9/12

Before: check_free_slots: "Gets availability." The agent called get_salon_info for "Are you free Saturday at 2?" because "availability" sounded like opening hours.

After: "Returns the free appointment times for one date. Use it whenever a customer asks if they can book or come at a time. Input date as YYYY-MM-DD. Not for opening hours; use get_salon_info for those."

Calculator fix: system message now says "Always use the calculator when a customer asks about more than one service."

The third calculator question ("Braids plus wash, how much?") was answered by the model adding ₦18,000 and ₦4,500 in its head. The answer was right, but the trace showed no calculator call, so it counts as the wrong tool.

Second run: 12/12. Each fix changed one description or one rule, and all 12 questions were re-run unchanged. Submit: the four descriptions on paper (photo), the 12-question table for both runs, before-and-after descriptions, and three trace screenshots.
mistakes: Fewer than two tools being their own workflows (all four are plain app nodes).
Two tools with overlapping jobs, so the agent keeps picking the wrong one and no description can fix it.
Rewording the test questions between runs to make the score go up.
Logging only the final score, without before-and-after descriptions.
g.pass: Exactly four tools, at least two of them sub-workflows, 12 questions (three per tool) with the tool chosen recorded per question, a final score of at least 11 of 12, and before-and-after descriptions in the log.
g.redo: Send it back if the score is under 11 of 12, there are fewer than two workflow tools, questions changed between runs, or no description changes are shown.
